standard_prerequisites.name: Base change in terms of injectives for torsion sheaves
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the reformulation of the base change property through injective sheaves of Z/ellZ-modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the form of the property used throughout: it suffices that the higher direct images of the relevant injective sheaves vanish after base change.

standard_prerequisites.name: Base change for the pushforward along a proper morphism

standard_prerequisites.name: The relative Leray spectral sequence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cohomology on Sites, the relative Leray spectral sequence for a composition of morphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the spectral sequence R^p g'_* R^q f'_* -> R^{p+q}(g' o f')_* whose vanishing input gives the conclusion.

core_obligations: Reduce to a pushforward of an injective (proof lines 18442-18453): fix a prime ell and an injective sheaf I of Z/ellZ-modules on Y; choose an injection f^{-1}I -> J with J injective on X; surjectivity of f makes I -> f_*J injective on stalks, and injectivity of I makes I a direct summand of f_*J, so it suffices to prove the vanishing for f_*J.

Set up the base change square (proof lines 18455-18462): for Z' -> Z put Y' = Z' x_Z Y and X' = Z' x_Z X = Y' x_Y X, with projections a, b, c and the base-changed f', g'; the pushforward base change lemma gives b^{-1}f_*J = f'_*a^{-1}J.
Apply the hypotheses (proof lines 18463-18470): by assumption the higher direct images R^q f'_*a^{-1}J vanish for q > 0 and so do the R^q(g' o f')_*a^{-1}J.

Conclude by the Leray spectral sequence (proof lines 18471-18474): the relative Leray spectral sequence R^p g'_* R^q f'_* a^{-1}J => R^{p+q}(g' o f')_*a^{-1}J degenerates because the q > 0 entries vanish, giving the vanishing of R^p g'_*(f'_*a^{-1}J) = R^p g'_* b^{-1}f_*J for p > 0, which is the base change property for g.
proof_roadmap: Replace an injective sheaf on Y by a direct summand of f_*J for an injective J on X, using surjectivity of f.
Pull the base change square back and use the base change formula for the pushforwards along f.
Degenerate the relative Leray spectral sequence using the two vanishing hypotheses to conclude the vanishing for g.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a sandwich property for base change: hypotheses on f and on g o f, together with surjectivity of f, give the property for g (statement lines 18430-18439). The proof (proof lines 18441-18474) reduces to proving the vanishing for a pushforward f_*J with J injective, using surjectivity of f to make I a direct summand of f_*J, and then degenerates the relative Leray spectral sequence for the base-changed composite g' o f' whose two inputs vanish by the two hypotheses. H2: one reduction plus one spectral-sequence degeneration, written out.
